summary: Design fan-out for the WebGL terrain lighting rebuild: 4 single-axis proposers + 3-persona judge panel

proposals.axis: WebGL terrain core — shader architecture replacing the baked-bitmap blit
proposals.summary: A WebGL2 underlayer canvas replaces the 4096² baked-bitmap blit with one fullscreen-triangle draw: a CPU-baked UNLIT albedo (the existing bake minus its lighting terms, so all 26 landcover characters survive pixel-for-pixel) modulated per-fragment by live sun lighting computed from a 512² R32F heightmap. Normals reproduce topo.ts's exact forward-difference math in-shader, so relief is computed at screen resolution — sharper than today at every zoom. Cast ridge shadows come from a GPU ray-marched sun-visibility map rebaked into a 1024² R8 FBO only when the sun moves (≤4 Hz), costing one texture tap per frame — this is what makes the valley read like Restrepo aerial footage: east-wall shadow flooding the floor at 0700, crawling up the west wall by 1700. The sun model (lat 34.8°N, fixed summer declination) is calibrated so the sun is below the horizon exactly when solarLight() is at starlight; gameplay light functions are untouched. The 2D canvas keeps contours, paths, night wash, and everything above — pixel-identical stacking — and the old lit-bake path stays alive as the no-WebGL fallback, keeping every existing headless harness green. Deploy eventually gets ~2-3 s faster via an optional Phase-4 GLSL port of the albedo bake (render-to-texture, validated by perceptual diff). Per-frame GPU cost is ~1-3 ms on integrated graphics against a 16.6 ms budget; texture memory ~92 MB. Reserved uniform/texture slots (cloud-shadow sampler defaulting to 1×1 white, height-fog params defaulting to today's haze, lift/gain grade hooks) let the atmosphere and grade axes plug in without touching the core shader.

key_decisions.decision: Hybrid texture pipeline: CPU-baked UNLIT albedo (4096² RGBA8, the existing bake minus its lighting/grade/haze terms) sampled by a GPU lighting shader; full GLSL albedo bake deferred to an optional Phase 4 behind a perceptual-diff gate
key_decisions.alternatives: (a) Full per-frame GLSL procedural landcover — rejected: the 26-class character is tuned and load-bearing, JS hash2 semantics (double-precision int32 coercion past 2^53) cannot be ported bit-exactly to uint GLSL, and per-frame fbm at 8 M fragments wastes the iGPU budget; (b) keep the lit bake — rejected, DECIDED the sun is live
key_decisions.rationale: Character survives pixel-for-pixel with near-zero porting risk (the albedo loop is a strict subset of code that already ships), while lighting/shadows/grade become live on the GPU; deploy speed is recovered later by the validated GPU bake rather than gambled up front

key_decisions.decision: Heightmap as 512² R32F with NEAREST filtering and manual bilinear via 4 texelFetch, replicating Terrain.elevAt's exact cell-corner lattice (clamp to size-1.001, no half-texel offset); normals computed in-shader with the bake's forward-difference-at-one-cell math (topo.ts:155-165)
key_decisions.alternatives: R16F + hardware LINEAR — rejected on arithmetic: 10-bit mantissa over a 1230 m range gives ~0.6 m quantization → ±0.12 rise/run normal banding; OES_texture_float_linear — rejected as a device-dependent branch; precomputed normal texture — rejected as a second source of truth (12 L1-cached texelFetches are effectively free, and per-fragment normals beat any fixed-resolution normal map at close zoom)
key_decisions.rationale: Bit-faithful height sampling keeps the GL relief registered to the 2D contours drawn from the same array on the canvas above — any lattice mismatch reads as contours sliding off the terrain; identical behavior on every GPU and SwiftShader

key_decisions.decision: Cast ridge shadows via a GPU ray-marched sun-visibility map rebaked into a 1024² R8 FBO only when the sun moves >0.25° (throttled ≤4 Hz); one bilinear tap per frame in the terrain shader; soft penumbra from max-occlusion-tangent + smoothstep
key_decisions.alternatives: Per-fragment per-frame ray-march — rejected: ~1.9 G texture fetches/frame at 1080p dpr2, hostile to integrated GPUs and fatal on SwiftShader; horizon-map precompute (16-32 azimuth sectors) — rejected: JS sweep precompute or extra GPU passes at deploy, 4 packed RGBA8 textures, and azimuth-sector interpolation artifacts at shadow edges, all to approximate what a 1-3 ms rebake computes exactly for the current sun
key_decisions.rationale: Amortized cost is noise (≤4 bakes/s of a ~1-3 ms pass), the per-frame cost is one tap, the result is exact for the live sun azimuth, and at high time-warp the shadow line visibly sweeps the valley — the marquee effect

key_decisions.decision: Keep the 2D lit-bake path fully alive as the no-WebGL fallback, selected once at mount; night wash stays on the 2D top canvas (pixel-identical stacking) with a u_nightMix GPU hook reserved for the grade axis
key_decisions.alternatives: Delete the 2D path — rejected: every headless harness runs --disable-gpu today and their screenshot baselines stay valid only on the 2D path; blacklisted drivers and context loss need a landing spot; moving night to GPU now — rejected because the wash sits OVER contours/paths and UNDER decoration (topo.ts:587-592), and replicating that stacking on the GPU buys nothing until the grade axis owns night
key_decisions.rationale: Zero-risk rollout: ok=false (or context loss) reverts to today's renderer byte-identical at one branch point; harness ecology untouched; night regression impossible in Phases 1-3

key_decisions.decision: Render-layer sun model in lib/render/gl/sun.ts: φ=34.8°N, fixed declination +20° (high-summer fighting season), solar noon 12:00 → sunrise ~05:04 / sunset ~18:56, with the direct term fading over 0-4° altitude
key_decisions.alternatives: Deriving sun altitude by inverting solarLight() — rejected: solarLight is a piecewise gameplay ramp with no azimuth, useless for shadow geometry; modeling calendar seasons — rejected: no season system exists (verified) and a drifting sunset would silently decouple from the fixed solarLight ramps

key_decisions.decision: One fullscreen-triangle draw call with a fixed uniform/texture contract: units 0-4 assigned, cloud-shadow sampler defaulting to 1×1 white, fog/grade uniforms defaulting to today's haze/identity — the atmosphere and grade axes extend TerrainEnv, never the shader plumbing

proposals.perf_budget: Per-frame GPU (terrain pass, 1 draw call): at 1920×1080 css × dpr 2 = 8.3 M fragments; per fragment ~14 height texelFetches (3 manual bilinears for normal + reuse for alt/fog), 1 trilinear albedo tap, 1 shadow tap, 1 cloud tap, ~100 ALU ops → ~1 GFLOP + ~120 M fetches/frame. The 512² R32F heightmap (1 MB) sits entirely in L2, so fetches are cache hits. Estimated 0.5-1.5 ms on Apple M1, 2-4 ms on Intel Iris Xe — against a 16.6 ms budget shared with a 2D pass that today sustains 116 fps WITH the 4096² drawImage blit it now sheds. Shadow rebake: 1024² × 56 steps × 4 fetches ≈ 235 M fetches ≈ 1-3 ms GPU, fired ≤4 Hz (typically once per game-minute) → ≤12 ms/s amortized, invisible. CPU per frame: ~20 uniform writes + 1-2 draw calls, < 0.05 ms; no per-frame texture uploads ever. Texture memory: albedo 4096² RGBA8 + mips ≈ 89 MB, height 1 MB, shadow 1-2 MB, landcover 0.25 MB → ~92 MB total (one-time, within iGPU shared-memory norms; the old path's 4096² canvas held ~67 MB in RAM anyway). proposals.summary: A single new pure render-layer module, lib/render/atmosphere.ts, turns world.secondsOfDay + weather into a complete SkyState: a physically-derived sun direction for a 34.8°N valley fixed at mid-July (declination +21°, the Korengal fighting season — and the one declination whose geometric sunrise 04:58/sunset 19:02 lands within minutes of the untouched gameplay solarLight() ramps at 05:00/19:30), plus sun/sky/moon colors keyed to sun altitude, a fixed anti-solar gibbous moon that rides the southern sky all night, and a shared color grade. The GL terrain underlayer consumes SkyState as uniforms (lighting combine, cached cast-shadow texture refreshed on a 0.5° sun-motion threshold so time-warp becomes a visible shadow time-lapse); the 2D top canvas consumes the same numbers via one source-atop tint fillRect inserted before drawNightLights and the HUD, so sprites grade coherently while map ink stays ungraded and additive muzzle/tracer light still punches through the dark. The flat navy night wash at topo.ts:587 dies, replaced by real low-key moonlight with the same target luminance (~0.3 of day) so legibility never regresses. A deliberate bonus falls out of the math: the evening sun sits at azimuth 287–296° (WNW), so the dynamic light converges on the ART_BIBLE's baked NW sprite key exactly at golden hour — the baked sprite art is "perpetual golden hour," and the worst mismatch (morning ENE) coincides with the least-visible shadows. The result clears the realism bar because it reproduces the single most documented visual fact about the Korengal: the sun line walking down the west wall at dawn and the floor staying in ridge shadow until mid-morning, on the live clock.

# Sun, Sky & Time-of-Day Color Model — Design

**Axis owner deliverables:** `lib/render/atmosphere.ts` (the model + API), the 2D screen-grade pass, the night relight (wash removal), the shadow-refresh *policy* (the terrain axis owns the shadow *pass* itself), and the consistency proof against `solarLight()`.

---

## 0. Component map & data flow

```
lib/sim/world/world.ts            (UNTOUCHED: solarLight/ambientLight/isNight/secondsOfDay)
        │  w.secondsOfDay, w.solarLight(), w.state.weather   (read-only, once per frame)
        ▼
lib/render/atmosphere.ts  [NEW — pure, deterministic, React-free, no wall clock, no random]
        │  SkyState { sunDir, sunColor, sunIntensity, skyColor, groundColor, skyIntensity,
        │             moonDir, moonColor, moonFactor, shadowStrength, nightFactor,
        │             grade{exposure, whiteBalance, saturation, lift, spriteTint},
        │             cloudShadowDensity, fogColor, spriteShadow{dx,dy,alpha} }
        ├──────────────► GL terrain underlayer (other axis): uniforms, every frame
        │                 └─ shadow FBO pass: rebaked only when sunDir moves > 0.5° (policy here)
        └──────────────► 2D top canvas (WorldView.draw):
                          • drawWeather / drawCop / drawNightLights night param → sky.nightFactor
                          • drawScreenGrade(ctx, cam, sky.grade.spriteTint)  ← NEW seam,
                            after all world content, BEFORE drawNightLights & HUD
```

One `skyState()` call per frame in `WorldView.draw()`; the result is passed down. Nothing in `lib/sim` changes. Determinism: the model is a pure function of `(secondsOfDay, weather, solar)` — same seed + same clock ⇒ same pixels (screenshot harness can pin the hour).

---

## 1. Sun-position model

**Fixed season: mid-July (day-of-year ≈ 196), solar declination δ = +21.0°.** Justification: (a) the Korengal's visual identity — *Restrepo*'s Battle Company footage and the OP Restrepo establishing shots — is the summer fighting season; *The Outpost*'s Kamdesh fight is October, but the campaign opens at the tempo peak, which is June–September; (b) measured fit: δ=21° is the declination whose geometry agrees with the untouched gameplay curve (proof below). Latitude φ = 34.8°N (Kunar). The game clock is treated as **local apparent solar time** (no equation of time, no UTC+4:30 — the clock IS the sun; document, don't model).

Hour angle `H = (secondsOfDay/3600 − 12) · 15°` (0 at solar noon, positive afternoon).

Standard equatorial→horizontal transform, in a local **E/N/U** frame:

```
sinAlt = sinφ·sinδ + cosφ·cosδ·cosH
east   = −cosδ·sinH
north  =  cosφ·sinδ − sinφ·cosδ·cosH
```

**World-frame mapping — the load-bearing sign:** world is `+x = east, +y = SOUTH` (y=0 is the north valley mouth; `worldToScreen` topo.ts:12-13 maps +y to screen-down, so north is up on screen). Therefore the **unit vector from surface toward the sun in WORLD coords** is:

```ts
// lib/render/atmosphere.ts
const DEG = Math.PI / 180;
const LAT = 34.8 * DEG;          // Kunar
const DECL = 21.0 * DEG;         // fixed mid-July (fighting season) — see consistency table
const sinPhi = Math.sin(LAT), cosPhi = Math.cos(LAT);
const sinDec = Math.sin(DECL), cosDec = Math.cos(DECL);

/** Unit vector surface→sun, world frame (+x E, +y S, +z up). Same convention as the
 *  old bake key (-0.55,-0.62,0.56) = "toward the NW sky" (−x west, −y north, +z up). */
export function sunDirWorld(secondsOfDay: number): [number, number, number] {
  const H = (secondsOfDay / 3600 - 12) * 15 * DEG;
  const cosH = Math.cos(H);
  const sinAlt = sinPhi * sinDec + cosPhi * cosDec * cosH;   // = sun z (up)
  const east = -cosDec * Math.sin(H);                         // = sun x
  const north = cosPhi * sinDec - sinPhi * cosDec * cosH;     // world y = SOUTH ⇒ negate
  return [east, -north, sinAlt]; // unit by construction (rotation of a unit vector)
}
```

**Verified table** (computed, not estimated — `node` check run against a copy of `solarLight()`):

| 05:00 | +0.4° | 64° | (+0.902, −0.432, +0.006) | 0.05 (ramp starts) |
| 06:00 | +11.8° | 73° | (+0.934, −0.294, +0.205) | 0.53 |
| 07:00 | +23.8° | 80° | (+0.902, −0.156, +0.403) | 1.00 (full) |

**Consistency proof (the contract):** sun is below the geometric horizon whenever `solarLight()` sits at the 0.05 starlight floor (sunrise 04:58 vs ramp start 05:00; sunset 19:02 with civil glow dying at 19:35 vs ramp floor 19:30). `isNight()` flips at sun alt +1.5° (dusk) / +6° (dawn) — within minutes of the geometric events. The 05:00–07:00 gameplay ramp gets a *literal* mechanism: sun at 6–24° altitude casts ridge shadows 0.8–3.7 km long, so the valley floor sits in cast shadow under a bright ambient sky until ~08:00 — exactly the documented Korengal morning, while gameplay "full light at 07:00" stays true because shadowed ground is ambient-lit (shadowStrength caps below, never black). **Sanity anchors:** noon sun is in the SOUTH (+y world, shadows point north/up-screen, both valley walls lit, short shadows); 08:00 sun in the EAST lights the west wall; evening sun is **WNW (287–296°) — it converges on the ART_BIBLE's baked NW sprite key at golden hour** (the baked sprite art is "perpetual golden hour"; the only true mismatch is morning ENE, when sprite shadows are smallest on screen).

Module-level constants of interest exported for docs/probes: `SUNRISE_H = 4.968`, `SUNSET_H = 19.032`, `CIVIL_DUSK_H = 19.585`.

## 2. Light-color ramps (sun, sky hemisphere, weather folding)

All colors are linear-ish sRGB triplets 0..1, restrained to the ART_BIBLE dust palette (±10% rule: the grade and light tints shift hue mildly; albedo stays canonical). **Weather folding — each gameplay multiplier maps to two visual knobs**, so total luminance tracks `ambientLight()` semantics exactly once (no double-darkening):

```ts
// directMult kills the BEAM (and with it cast shadows); exposure carries the gameplay total.
const WX: Record<string, { direct: number; cloudShadow: number }> = {
  Clear: { direct: 1.0, cloudShadow: 0.0 },  Hazy: { direct: 0.8, cloudShadow: 0.25 },
  Overcast: { direct: 0.15, cloudShadow: 0.85 }, Rain: { direct: 0.08, cloudShadow: 0.9 },
  Fog: { direct: 0.05, cloudShadow: 0.2 },   Snow: { direct: 0.2, cloudShadow: 0.6 },
};
sunIntensity = baseIntensity(alt) * WX[w.label].direct;
skyIntensity = baseSky(alt) * lerp(1.25, 1.0, WX[w.label].direct);   // overcast = flatter, softer
grade.exposure = baseExposure(alt) * weatherLightMult(w);            // import from lib/sim/campaign
shadowStrength = baseShadow(alt) * WX[w.label].direct;               // overcast ⇒ shadows melt away
nightFactor = 1 - clamp01(solar * weatherLightMult(w));              // EXACTLY today's `night`
```
`weatherLightMult` is imported from `lib/sim/campaign.ts:186` (render importing sim functions is established practice — combat-fx.ts already imports sim types). `solar` is passed in by the caller (`w.solarLight()`), so the gameplay curve is **never duplicated** in the render layer.

`shadowStrength` base: 0.55 high day → 0.65 at golden hour (alt < 10°) → 0.5 under moon. Hard legibility cap: shadowed terrain receives full hemisphere ambient, so day shade ≥ ~0.45× lit luma — the tactical read survives everywhere (legibility > realism, per contract).

## 3. Night — moon, starlight, and the death of the navy wash

**Moon (decided): fixed anti-solar gibbous.** Hour angle `Hm = H − 180°`, declination δm = −18°, illumination factor 0.65. Verified: moonrise ≈ 19:00, transit 37° due south at 00:00, moonset ≈ 05:00 — **up for essentially the entire night**, riding low across the southern sky with long raking shadows (a low summer moon is astronomically correct: a near-full moon mirrors the sun's declination). Rationale: a permanently-up moon maximizes night-ops readability and makes night terrain *gorgeous* instead of flat; phase realism (illum cycles) buys nothing the sim reads and costs a dark-night legibility floor problem. `moonColor = (0.70, 0.78, 0.95)`, `moonIntensity = 0.10 × 0.65 × clamp01(moonAlt/12°) × WX.direct` — overcast kills moonlight and its shadows, exactly like the sun.

**Starlight floor:** hemisphere ambient row at alt ≤ −12° above, ×`weatherLightMult`. Hard floor on terrain mean luma ≈ **0.12 of day** (moonless + overcast worst case) — never illegible.

**Replacing topo.ts:587-592 (the flat `rgba(8,14,30, .35+night*.42)` wash):**
- **Terrain (GL):** the lighting equation simply *continues* at night — key light = moon (real cast shadows from the same shadow path, moon direction), ambient = starlight. Target mean luminance ≈ 0.30 of day with moon up (matches today's wash result of ~0.37, slightly darker but with *form*), cool white-balance and scotopic desaturation from the grade (§4). The relief survives the night: ridges still shade, the moon line still moves.

## 4. The full-screen time-of-day grade — **dual-pass, shared math** (decision)

CSS filter on a wrapper is rejected (it would grade the in-canvas HUD ink and React chrome, and offers only coarse hue-rotate/sepia controls). A single source-over veil on the top canvas is rejected (it's the flat-wash contrast-killer we're deleting). **Chosen: grade each canvas with the same numbers from atmosphere.ts:**

**(a) Terrain canvas — graded in the GL fragment shader** (free; it's where the light already lives):

```glsl
uniform float uExposure;      // baseExposure(alt) * weatherLightMult — gameplay-consistent
uniform vec3  uWhiteBalance;  // per-channel gain
uniform float uSaturation;    // 1.0 day → 0.45 deep night (scotopic)
uniform vec3  uLift;          // shadow-region tint (blue-hour/dawn shadows)

vec3 grade(vec3 c) {
  c *= uExposure * uWhiteBalance;
  float l = dot(c, vec3(0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722));
  c = mix(vec3(l), c, uSaturation);
  c += uLift * (1.0 - clamp(l, 0.0, 1.0));   // lifts/tints shadows only, highlights untouched
  return c;
}
```

Grade keyframes (same altitude-lerped table):

| band | exposure (Clear) | whiteBalance | saturation | lift | spriteTint (r,g,b,a) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| high day (alt ≥ 30°) | 1.00 | (1, 1, 1) | 1.00 | (0,0,0) | a = 0 (pass skipped) |
| afternoon (10°) | 0.97 | (1.04, 0.99, 0.93) | 1.03 | (0,0,0) | (255,196,140, 0.05) |
| golden (2–6°) | 0.90 | (1.10, 0.92, 0.78) | 1.08 | (0.02, 0.01, 0.00) | (255,176,112, 0.12) |
| civil twilight (−4°) | 0.55 | (0.88, 0.92, 1.10) | 0.80 | (0.01, 0.02, 0.05) | (70, 86, 130, 0.20) |
| night (≤ −10°) | 0.32 | (0.78, 0.85, 1.12) | 0.45 | (0.01, 0.02, 0.06) | (14, 20, 38, 0.42) |

(The golden WB (1.10,0.92,0.78) is a ≤10% hue push — inside the ART_BIBLE tint-restraint line; the dust palette warms, it doesn't become Instagram.)

**(b) Top canvas — one `source-atop` tint fillRect**, NEW function in a new file (it's atmosphere's output, not topo's):

```ts
// lib/render/atmosphere.ts
/** Grade the 2D world layer: lerps every ALREADY-DRAWN pixel toward the tint without
 *  touching alpha — transparent areas stay transparent (the GL terrain below is NOT
 *  veiled; it grades itself in-shader with the same table). Cost: one composite op.  */
export function drawScreenGrade(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, cam: Camera, t: SpriteTint) {
  if (t.a < 0.01) return;                       // clear midday: literally free
  ctx.save();
  ctx.globalCompositeOperation = "source-atop"; // C' = a·T + (1−a)·C, alpha preserved
  ctx.fillStyle = `rgba(${t.r},${t.g},${t.b},${t.a})`;
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, cam.vw, cam.vh);
  ctx.restore();
}
```

Why `source-atop` is the load-bearing choice: `multiply`/`soft-light` blend modes composite source-over, so on the now transparent-backed top canvas they'd paint a flat veil over the see-through regions and re-create the navy-wash bug on top of the GL terrain. `source-atop` is the only op that grades **only drawn pixels** and preserves alpha exactly. The lerp-toward-tint is a good mid-tone approximation of the shader grade for sprite-sized content; coherence comes from both passes reading one keyframe table. **Legibility guards:** tint alpha hard-capped at 0.5 (faction accents must survive deepest night — the GL terrain carries the darkness, not the sprites); seam placed before `drawNightLights` and the HUD block so additive gun-light and all ink/HUD stay ungraded.

## 6. GLSL — the terrain shader terms this axis owns

Heightmap orientation contract: `elev` rows upload in cy order ⇒ texture **v = wy / worldSize with NO flip** (row 0 = north = y 0). Formats per the hazard: heightmap **R32F + NEAREST** (manual 4-tap bilinear where smooth sampling matters — avoids the OES_texture_float_linear dependency AND the R16F precision trap: half-float ulp at 2 km elevation is 1–2 m, which would terrace the normals); normals precomputed CPU-side once into RGBA8 (8-bit normals are fine at 5 m cells; same central-difference as topo.ts:157-165).

```glsl
// --- normal (from the baked normal texture; matches the old bake's convention) -------
vec3 n = normalize(texture(uNormalTex, vUV).xyz * 2.0 - 1.0);   // world frame, +z up

// --- cast-shadow: ray-march the heightmap toward the key light (sun or moon) ---------
// Runs in the SHADOW FBO PASS, not per-frame: rebaked only when keyDir moves > 0.5°.
float castShadow(vec2 wpos, vec3 toKey) {              // wpos in meters
  if (toKey.z <= 0.02) return 0.0;                     // body at/below horizon: all shadow
  float stepM = uShadowStepM;                          // ~2 texels: 10 m (5 m headless)
  vec2  dxy   = normalize(toKey.xy) * stepM;
  float dzds  = toKey.z / length(toKey.xy) * stepM;    // ray rise per step (m)
  float rayH  = heightAt(wpos) + 1.0;                  // 1 m bias kills self-shadow acne
  float soft  = 0.0;
  for (int i = 1; i <= 48; i++) {                      // 48·10 m = 480 m reach ≈ max ridge throw at alt>9°;
    vec2 p = wpos + dxy * float(i);                    // below that the floor is fully shadowed anyway
    rayH += dzds;
    soft = max(soft, clamp((heightAt(p) - rayH) * 0.25, 0.0, 1.0)); // soft penumbra, no aliasing
    if (soft >= 1.0) break;
  }
  return 1.0 - soft;                                   // 1 = lit, stored in uShadowTex (R8, 1024²)
}

// --- lighting combine (main terrain fragment, every frame) ---------------------------
float lit    = texture(uShadowTex, vUV).r;             // cached; keyed to uKeyDir
float shadow = mix(1.0 - uShadowStrength, 1.0, lit);   // shadowed ground keeps full ambient below
float sunNL  = max(dot(n, uSunDir), 0.0);
float moonNL = max(dot(n, uMoonDir), 0.0);
float skyVis = 0.5 + 0.5 * n.z;                        // hemisphere visibility = the bake's old `sky` term
vec3 direct  = uSunColor  * (uSunIntensity * sunNL)  * shadow
             + uMoonColor * (uMoonFactor  * moonNL)  * shadow;
vec3 ambient = mix(uGroundColor, uSkyColor, skyVis) * uSkyIntensity;
vec3 color   = albedo.rgb * (direct + ambient);        // albedo = de-shaded 4096² bake (terrain axis)

// optional Phase-4 flourish: the sun made visible on water (river mask in albedo.a)
float glint  = pow(max(dot(reflect(-uSunDir, n), vec3(0,0,1)), 0.0), 48.0);
color += albedo.a * glint * uSunColor * uSunIntensity * 0.6;

fragColor = vec4(grade(color), 1.0);                   // grade() from §4
```

**Albedo contract with the terrain axis (hard requirement):** the 4096² bake keeps landcover color, procedural `tex` detail, snow line, and saturation lifts, but **drops the `shade` term entirely** (topo.ts:169-173 — key/fill/sky move into the shader above). Shipping a lit albedo under this shader double-shades every slope. Altitude haze moves to the fog axis.

**Shadow-refresh policy (this axis owns the schedule):** rebake `uShadowTex` when `dot(prevKeyDir, keyDir) < cos(0.5°)` or the key body swaps (sun↔moon — the swap happens while both are near zero intensity, so it's invisible). Sun moves 0.25°/min ⇒ at 1× one 1024² rebake per ~2 min of game time (~free); at 60× warp one per ~2 s — and the sweeping shadow line becomes the *feature*: time-warp is a visible shadow time-lapse, the master clock made literal. Cap at one rebake per 2 frames so extreme warp can't stack passes. Headless/SwiftShader: 512² shadow tex + 5 m steps via the existing `--webgl` flag plumbing in scripts/visual-matrix.mjs.

## 9. Residual risk deliberately taken

The static sprite library keeps its baked NW key light and SE cast shadows (164 SVGs are NOT re-authored). The dynamic terrain sun matches them exactly at golden hour, acceptably at noon (short shadows), and contradicts them at dawn (sun ENE) — accepted because morning sprite shadows are sub-8-px at typical zoom, and the sun-tracking *procedural* contact shadows (separate axis, fed by `spriteShadow`) carry the directional read. proposals.axis: atmosphere — cloud shadows, terrain-aware valley fog, aerial perspective, and the evolution of the 2D weather layer
proposals.summary: The atmosphere layer makes the valley breathe: a world-anchored two-octave cloud-shadow field (CPU-baked tileable FBM texture, sampled in the terrain fragment shader) drifts with the live windVector and the master clock — sparse hard-edged cumulus shadows on Clear days, broad soft mottle under Overcast, frozen when paused and racing like timelapse at 8x warp, with sun-parallax projection off weather.ceiling so ridge tops sit closer to the deck than the river. Valley fog becomes physically pooled: a once-baked 128-square "local valley floor" min-field plus a diurnal radiation-fog schedule (mist builds after midnight, peaks at dawn in the 1550-1700 m river draw, burns off by 09:30 — consistent with solarLight()'s 07:00 full-sun) gives per-pixel exponential transmittance through the fog layer; Fog weather drives depth straight from weather.ceiling (300 m), reproducing the Korengal inversion layer with ridges poking out — and visually explaining airAvailable=false. The 2D layer stays consistent via one shared TS module: fogVisAt(wx,wy) samples the SAME Float32 floor-field and noise arrays the GPU uses, so sprites/decoration fade with the fog while tactical symbology is clamped to a 0.55 alpha floor (legibility never loses). The baked warm-low/cool-high haze (topo.ts:298-309) moves into the shader as live aerial perspective, now weather- and zoom-aware. drawWeather sheds its veil and fog blobs (replaced by GL terms) and keeps only the crisp screen-space precip particles, which remain wall-clock. Cheap extras land as two albedo uniforms: sim-clock-integrated ground wetness during/after precip and a dynamic snow line that descends from the baked 68% cap toward 40% during Snow weather. All parameters are low-pass filtered over ~90 s of sim time so the 4-9 h weather re-rolls roll in instead of popping. Cost: 4 small-texture fetches + ~40 ALU per terrain pixel and 144 KB of texture — well inside budget next to the lighting axis's shadow march, and the 2D canvas actually gets cheaper (fullscreen gradient blobs deleted).

key_decisions.decision: Cloud noise = one-time CPU-baked 256-square tileable two-channel FBM texture (RG8, LINEAR, REPEAT), sampled twice in the terrain shader with wind-scrolled world-space UVs
key_decisions.alternatives: Live hash-FBM in GLSL (rejected: ~100+ ALU/pixel, crawls on the SwiftShader headless harness path; buys nothing visually over a scrolled texture). Per-frame CPU-rendered scrolling shadow canvas uploaded as a texture (rejected: per-frame texSubImage upload + CPU fill for something two texture fetches do free).
key_decisions.rationale: Two fetches from a 64 KB always-resident texture + a smoothstep is ~6 ALU, deterministic (fixed-seed bake, no Math.random), works on integrated GPUs and SwiftShader, and retaining the Float32 source array gives the 2D layer an exact-parity CPU sampler for free.

key_decisions.decision: Cloud advection uses sim-clock (CPU-integrated offset += windVector x delta(world.state.clock)); precip particles stay wall-clock
key_decisions.alternatives: Wall-clock clouds (rejected: at 8x warp the DECIDED master-clock sun sweeps fast while clouds crawl - incoherent; and clouds moving during pause contradicts the frozen sun). Closed-form clock x wind phase (rejected: weather re-rolls every 4-9 h change windDir discontinuously and would teleport every shadow; integration just bends streamlines).
key_decisions.rationale: World-anchored phenomena follow world time: pause = still photo (good planning feedback), 8x warp = timelapse clouds racing with the terminator (the cheapest available 'holy shit' moment). Screen-space precip on wall-clock keeps the UI visibly alive during pause.

key_decisions.decision: Fog pooling is computed against a baked 128-square 'local valley floor' min-filtered elevation field, with depth = f(time-of-day, weather) ABOVE that local floor, and transmittance = exp(-k x thickness) closed-form per pixel
key_decisions.alternatives: Fixed MSL fog ceiling (rejected: the river floor rises 1550 to 2000 m south - a fixed ceiling drowns the north half and never fogs the south draw). Volumetric ray-march (rejected: pointless for an orthographic top-down camera where the path length through a pooled layer IS the layer thickness - closed form is exact, not an approximation).
key_decisions.rationale: The floor field makes fog hug the main river draw AND tributary draws automatically, reproducing the Korengal dawn inversion (ridges poking out of a 300 m fog deck under Fog weather, driven directly by the sim's weather.ceiling), for one 16 KB texture fetch and one exp().

key_decisions.decision: 2D sprite/fog consistency via one shared TS function (fogVisAt) sampling the SAME Float32 arrays the GPU textures were uploaded from, with per-class alpha floors (symbology never below 0.55)
key_decisions.alternatives: A second GL overlay canvas on top for fog (rejected: DECIDED says FX/units stay on the 2D canvas; adds a third canvas and compositing cost). Fading nothing (rejected: units floating bright over a white-out destroys the effect). Fading everything fully (rejected: the map must stay a legible tactical map - the sim's visibilityM perception gate already decides what you KNOW; what is drawn must stay readable).
key_decisions.rationale: Shared source arrays give exact parity (verified by a scratch parity harness), zero new canvases, and the class-based floors encode the legibility contract explicitly: scenery fogs out, symbology dims at most 45%.

key_decisions.decision: Baked altitude warm/cool + haze (topo.ts:296-309) deleted from makeBake and moved into the shader as live, weather- and zoom-aware aerial perspective; distance-from-camera desaturation NOT implemented
key_decisions.alternatives: Keeping the haze baked (rejected: it double-applies once GL fog/veil exist, and a baked haze cannot respond to visibilityM or zoom). Radial distance desat at strategic zoom (rejected: orthographic top-down camera - every pixel is equidistant, the effect is physically false here).
key_decisions.rationale: Same default coefficients (0.08 warm / 0.13 cool / ~10% floor haze) preserve the proven look at Phase B, then visibilityM scales haze strength (Hazy days show real depth grading) and a ppm-driven hazeK boost (1.35x at strategic) gives the honest version of 'pulling out adds air'.

key_decisions.decision: drawWeather keeps ONLY the precip particle system; veil and fog blobs are deleted (absorbed by GL veil uniform + real pooled fog); all atmosphere parameters low-pass filtered over ~90 s sim time
key_decisions.alternatives: Porting precip to GL points (rejected: screen-space frozen-grid vector streaks are exactly what the 2D canvas does well, and they sit at the same z-order today - under units - so nothing improves). Letting weather re-rolls switch params instantly (rejected: a 4-9 h re-roll would pop the whole sky in one frame).
key_decisions.rationale: The veil is a fullscreen fillRect that belongs in the shader for free; the blobs were a hand-drawn placeholder for exactly what the pooled fog now does physically; the low-pass makes fog ROLL IN over a minute, which is both more real and more dramatic.

risks.mitigation: Density cap 0.34 on Clear (shadows never approach the darkness of the cast ridge-shadow term), soft edges per label, 1800 m world-anchored shapes too large to alias with 5 m terrain features, and motion disambiguates in play; pause-frame review included in the Phase C screenshot matrix.

risks.mitigation: All atmosphere textures are 8-bit UNORM (RG8/R8) with LINEAR - universally filterable, no OES_texture_float_linear dependency; added cost is 4 small-texture fetches + ~40 ALU, dwarfed by the lighting axis's shadow march; visual-matrix.mjs --webgl (--use-angle=swiftshader) runs are a standing check from Phase B on.

proposals.perf_budget: GPU per frame (added by this axis to the terrain fragment shader): 4 fetches from tiny resident textures (256sq RG8 cloud tile = 128 KB, 128sq R8 floor field = 16 KB - both live in cache permanently) + ~40 ALU including one exp() and one clamped division, per terrain pixel. At 1920x1080 dpr1 (~2.1 MPix) on an Intel Iris Xe-class iGPU this is well under 0.5 ms - an estimated 10-15% increment on the terrain pass, whose cost is dominated by the lighting axis's ridge-shadow march, not these terms. At dpr2 (~8.3 MPix) it scales to ~1.5-2 ms worst case, still comfortably inside a 16.6 ms frame that today runs at ~116 fps with headroom. CPU per frame: atmo.step() is a few dozen float ops (offset integration, table lerp, low-pass) plus ~16 uniform uploads - microseconds; fogVisAt is called per world-anchored 2D draw (~100-300 calls/frame at tactical zoom), each ~20 float ops + one elevAt bilinear = well under 0.1 ms. One-time costs: cloud tile bake ~5 ms, floor-field bake (separable min+blur over 512sq, downsample) ~10-20 ms, both inside the existing multi-second deploy bake window. Texture memory added: 144 KB total - noise next to the 64 MB 4096sq albedo upload the GL core already budgets. The 2D canvas gets CHEAPER: the deleted fullscreen veil fillRect and up to 3 fullscreen radial-gradient blobs (among the slowest canvas2d ops) save an estimated 1-2 ms on Fog/Overcast frames. Net: atmosphere holds 60 fps with margin on integrated GPUs alongside the existing 2D pass, and the worst pre-existing frame (Fog weather) actually improves on the 2D side.

proposals.axis: art-seam — everything drawn ON TOP of the new WebGL terrain: sprite shadows, decoration, grade coherence, contours, hero assets, ART_BIBLE contract
proposals.summary: The 2D layer above the GL terrain gets one new physical system — sun-tracking cast shadows — and one new coherence system — a shared sun/grade module that both canvases read. Roughly 33 of the 164 sprites (vegetation, COP structures, qalats — the static world-fixed objects) have their baked SE shadows stripped from the SVG sources (wrapped in a `data-cast-shadow` group the manifest builder removes) and replaced by a runtime projected-silhouette shadow: a pre-baked, blurred, half-res tint of each sprite's own raster, slid and stretched along the live sun's shadow axis with length = castHeight·cot(elevation), clamped. This also fixes a latent bug: HESCO/ECP segments are drawn rotated today (draw.ts:404,445), so their baked "SE" shadows already point the wrong way around the ring. Rotating figures/vehicles keep their symmetric contact shadows (unchanged, per ART_BIBLE rationale); flat ink (markers/HUD/UI/FX, ~100 sprites) is untouched. Time-of-day grade and night dim reach sprites via a single full-screen 'source-atop' tint pass on the top canvas — the only composite op that tints existing pixels without occluding the GL terrain below — driven by the same gradeFor() function the GL shader receives as uniforms, so sprites never float off the graded terrain. Draw order is re-cut so world dressing (decoration, villages, COP) sits under weather+grade while units, orders, ink labels, and combat FX stay above (legibility law preserved); contours/paths/grid stay exactly as they are, just split out of drawTerrain. Fifteen hero sprites (qalats, mosque, B-huts/TOC, guard tower, HESCO, ECP, cedar/walnut, UH-60) get 2–4× re-authors with Kunar-correct detail (stone-and-timber qalats, plywood B-huts, wire-grid HESCO) and baked AO under the new soft-light contract. The result clears the bar because the one thing aerial footage of the Korengal always shows — long morning shadows raking west off every cedar and tower, swinging north by noon, dying under overcast — now happens, coherently, on both canvases at once.

key_decisions.decision: Strip baked cast shadows from ~33 static world sprites and draw a runtime projected self-silhouette shadow (pre-baked half-res blurred tint of the sprite's own raster, slid/stretched along the sun axis); keep symmetric contact shadows on all rotating figures/vehicles; leave all flat ink untouched.
key_decisions.alternatives: (a) Keep baked shadows everywhere and accept the dawn/dusk contradiction — rejected: thousands of tree shadows frozen NW against an east-raking GL terrain at 17:00 is the single loudest tell that the scene is fake, and the rotated HESCO/ECP segments already break the baked contract today (draw.ts:404,445). (b) Author 4-8 directional shadow variants per sprite — rejected: 33 sprites × N angles of hand art for what one transform does. (c) Dynamic shadows for soldiers too — rejected per ART_BIBLE rotation rationale and because a 1.4 m man's shadow at ≤26 px is sub-noise.
key_decisions.rationale: The silhouette projection is ~60 lines, costs one extra drawImage per instance, needs zero new art for the long tail, automatically handles rotated statics, and concentrates hand-authoring budget on the 15 heroes where it shows.

key_decisions.decision: Shadows draw interleaved (immediately under each sprite inside drawWorldSprite), not as a separate全-shadow pass.
key_decisions.alternatives: Two-pass (all shadows then all sprites) — cleaner in dense forest but requires restructuring drawCop and every call site; per-sun-bucket composite atlases (shadow+sprite pre-merged per 5° sun bucket) — zero per-frame cost but breaks on rotated sprites (HESCO ring) and adds cache complexity.
key_decisions.rationale: Interleaved matches exactly what today's baked shadows do under painter's y-sort (the accepted look), is a one-point change, and decoration.ts already collects items[] so lifting to two-pass later is a 6-line escape hatch if forest screenshots look dirty.

key_decisions.decision: Static sprite SURFACE shading stays baked with a softened NW form-light bias + AO; only CAST shadows become dynamic.
key_decisions.alternatives: Fully dynamic surface lighting via normal-mapped sprites in GL — rejected as a different (much larger) architecture; fully flattening surface shading to ambient-only — rejected because silhouettes lose volume at the §7 squint test.
key_decisions.rationale: Flat rasters can't be relit; cast shadows carry ~90% of the time-of-day read. Pairing the sprites' residual NW bias with the ~30% fixed NW form light gl-core should blend into terrain (also the relief-inversion fix) makes the residual bias a shared, coherent convention rather than a contradiction.

key_decisions.decision: Time-of-day grade and night dim reach sprites via ONE full-screen 'source-atop' fillRect on the top canvas, fed by the same gradeFor() function gl-core receives as mix() uniforms; world dressing (decoration/villages/COP structures) draws under it, units/ink/FX above it.
key_decisions.alternatives: multiply/overlay composite on the top canvas — WRONG: against transparent pixels it produces opaque fill that occludes the GL terrain. CSS filter on the canvas element — imprecise, can't match the GL curve, dpr-fragile. Per-sprite tinting — N offscreen composites per frame. Grading units too — rejected: legibility is law and today's units were never night-washed.
key_decisions.rationale: source-atop is the only canvas composite that tints existing pixels while preserving transparency; one quad, exact parity achievable by mandating GL use the identical alpha-mix form.

key_decisions.decision: One shared sun module lib/render/sun.ts (lat 34.8°N, fixed +15° declination, solar noon 12:15) is the single source of light truth for both canvases; sprite shadows, terrain lighting, grade, and fog all derive from it.
key_decisions.alternatives: Letting each axis model its own sun — guaranteed drift (sprite shadows pointing differently than ridge shadows is worse than no shadows); a full seasonal ephemeris — over-engineering for a fixed-season campaign.
key_decisions.rationale: Hand-verified against the sacred gameplay curve: sun crosses the horizon ~05:30/~19:05, below horizon whenever solarLight is at starlight; az 78° at 06:15 (shadows WSW), 180° at noon (shadows N, short), 282° at 18:30 — physically right for Kunar in fighting season and consistent with solarLight()'s 05-07/17-19.5 ramps without touching lib/sim.

key_decisions.decision: Occluding valley fog lives on the TOP canvas (drawWeather upgraded with a terrain-aware pooling weight); gl-core keeps only non-occluding surface haze.
key_decisions.alternatives: GL fog under the sprite layer — qalats and trees poke through fog banks, instantly fake; a third GL canvas above the 2D one — architecture cost far beyond the payoff.
key_decisions.rationale: Fog must hide trees and structures to read as fog; drawWeather's deterministic blob field already exists, already damps at night, and needs only a ~25-line elevation-pooling multiplier.

key_decisions.decision: Shadow markup stays in SVG sources wrapped in <g data-cast-shadow>, stripped at manifest build time, with castHeight in _meta.json validated against the wrap.
key_decisions.alternatives: Deleting shadow elements from sources — loses the audit trail and asset-bible comparability; runtime DOM-parsing strip — slow and fragile at boot.
key_decisions.rationale: Sources remain the single edited artifact per the generated-files invariant; the build step is 20 lines; the cross-validation (castHeight ⟺ data-cast-shadow) turns the two failure modes (double shadow / missing shadow) into build errors.

proposals.perf_budget: Per-frame GPU/CPU (top 2D canvas, integrated GPU): +1 small drawImage per shadow-casting instance. Typical views (COP or village, ~100-300 static sprites on screen): +0.3-0.9 ms. Worst case (close-zoom dense forest at the existing decoration CAP of 1800): +1800 textured-quad blits ≈ +2-4 ms on a GPU-accelerated canvas — today's frame is ~8.6 ms (116 fps via shoot.mjs --fps), so worst case lands ~11-13 ms ≈ 75-90 fps, and that view is rare; shadows are also fully OFF at night (~35-40% of clock time) and under fog/heavy overcast via shadowAlpha=0. Grade pass: one full-screen source-atop fillRect ≈ <0.3 ms. sunState/gradeFor: trivial trig, once per frame. Texture/canvas memory: shadow masks ~33 sprites at half base res (128-256 px) ≈ 4-5 MB; hero re-rasters at bumped res ≈ +8-10 MB sprite atlas; total +~15 MB against the existing 67 MB 4096² terrain bake (which this overhaul likely retires in CPU form) — net memory roughly flat or down. Load time: shadow-mask baking +60-150 ms folded into the existing assets phase with progress reporting; if gl-core goes GPU-procedural for albedo, the 2-3 s relief bake collapses to GL init + 512² heightmap upload + one warm-up render, so total deploy time goes DOWN. Escape hatches if the forest worst case measures hot: per-frame shadow cap on y-sorted items, or pre-composited shadow+sprite atlases per 5° sun bucket for the (non-rotated) vegetation family, which returns per-frame cost to exactly today's one blit per item. All numbers to be re-measured at P1 with shoot.mjs --fps before/after as the gate.
open_questions: Which axis owns lib/render/sun.ts in the synthesized plan? This design assumes the TS module is the single source and GL receives uniforms computed CPU-side per frame (no GLSL re-derivation) — synthesizer must dedupe if gl-core proposed its own model, and the gameplay-consistency constants (solar noon 12:15, decl +15°) must survive the merge.

Does gl-core keep a CPU albedo bake (loading phase stays seconds) or go GPU-procedural (phase collapses to <1 s)? renderWarmPhases here is designed for either behind prepareTerrainGPU(terrain, report), but the 'relief' phase label/reporting granularity should match the chosen path.

Will gl-core blend the recommended ~25-35% fixed NW form light into terrain diffuse (relief-inversion fix)? If not, the sprite surface-shading contract should drop its residual NW bias too (flatter ambient+AO) to avoid a one-sided convention.

Where does the noon-grade neutral point sit exactly? Sprites are authored to read correctly at zero grade; if gl-core's terrain look needs a nonzero midday tint, the sprite source-atop pass must mirror it (shared gradeFor handles this, but the art QA baseline screenshots should be taken at whatever 'neutral' the merged design picks.

Fog pooling occlusion of VILLAGE STRUCTURES vs the village name labels/pins: labels currently draw in the same village block (WorldView.tsx:324-335); design keeps labels above the grade+fog — confirm the synthesizer keeps label draws out of the fogged band when the village loop is split.

Should sprite shadows also respect GL ridge shadows (a tree inside a mountain's cast shadow shouldn't cast its own)? Correct answer is yes via sampling a coarse CPU shadow-factor grid from sunState ray-march, but it's a cross-canvas data dependency — proposed as a post-P2 polish question, not in scope here.

verdicts.persona: Staff graphics engineer (shipped WebGL/WebGPU renderers in browsers and games). Rubric: technical correctness (formats, filtering, precision, shadow math, DPR), per-frame cost honesty on integrated GPUs, robustness (context loss, SwiftShader headless), and whether phasing keeps the game working at every step. Ruthless about hand-waved GLSL and unstated texture memory.

proposal_reviews.axis: WebGL terrain core — shader architecture replacing the baked-bitmap blit
proposal_reviews.strengths: The strongest proposal and the right spine. Format discipline is exemplary: R32F + NEAREST + manual 4-texelFetch bilinear sidesteps the OES_texture_float_linear hazard AND the R16F precision trap with actual arithmetic (~0.6 m half-float quantization → ±0.12 rise/run normal banding — correct), and the heightAt GLSL is a verified bit-faithful port of Terrain.elevAt (same cell-corner lattice, clamp size-1.001) — I checked the cited topo.ts lighting constants (key*1.05 + fill*0.34 + sky*0.24, shade*0.94+0.02 at :169-173) and the shader transcription is term-for-term faithful. The unlit-albedo hybrid is the correct call: I verified the hash2 claim at topo.ts:83-87 — `(h^(h>>13)) * 1274126177` does exceed 2^53 before ToInt32, so a uint GLSL port is genuinely not bit-portable, and deferring the GPU albedo bake behind a perceptual-diff gate is exactly right risk allocation. The rebaked 1024² R8 sun-visibility FBO with exponential stride (5·1.13^k spans ~4.2 km — checks out) is the only shadow design in the set whose march actually reaches the occluding ridge. Perf accounting is honest and itemized (8.3 M frags × ~14 cache-hit texelFetches, 89 MB albedo+mips computed correctly, dpr-1.5 reserve lever named). Robustness is best-in-class: alive 2D fallback keeps every --disable-gpu harness baseline valid, context-loss handlers named, Phase-1 GL-blit-parity step proves canvas stack/DPR/camera math before any lighting lands. Phasing is the best of the four — every phase shippable, screenshot-diff gated.
proposal_reviews.weaknesses: The 'other axes plug in without touching the core shader' claim is overstated in two places. (1) The grade hook `col = col*u_gain + u_lift` cannot express the sky axis's saturation or per-channel white balance — the grade axis would reopen the core shader immediately. (2) The reserved cloud sampler — one tap, `texture(u_cloud, uv+u_cloudOff).r` multiplied into vis — cannot host the atmosphere axis's design (two scrolled octaves, coverage-threshold smoothstep, sun-parallax offset by per-pixel elevation, and a mottle term that multiplies AMBIENT, not direct). The shadow-bake policy keys only off the sun; the sky axis's moon (keyDir swap) has no input. No cliff/slope scalar is exposed for the atmosphere axis's wetness/snow terms. Albedo alpha semantics are unpinned (P2's river glint wants a mask there; a canvas upload gives opaque 255). Midday brightness calibration is honestly flagged but unresolved. Iris Xe estimate (2-4 ms at 8.3 Mpx with 12+ dependent fetches) is slightly optimistic — the reserve lever covers it.
must_fix: Replace the gain/lift grade hook with the sky axis's full grade() block (exposure, per-channel white balance, saturation, shadow lift) at identity defaults — gain+lift cannot express saturation/WB and the grade axis would otherwise reopen the 'sealed' core shader

Replace the reserved 1-tap cloud sampler with a chunk-splice contract: the core shader exposes worldM, elev, altNorm, N, sunVis, direct, ambient, albedo (and a derivable cliff/slope scalar) at named insertion points, and composes axis-owned GLSL chunks — the atmosphere axis's cloudField/mottle/fog terms cannot fit through one texture tap
Shadow-bake input becomes keyDir (sun OR moon, supplied by the sky module), not the sun — otherwise the night-relight axis forks the pass
Pin albedo alpha-channel semantics (opaque vs river mask) before bakeAlbedo ships — RGBA8 canvas upload yields alpha=255 and deciding later forces a re-bake

proposal_reviews.axis: Sun, sky, and time-of-day color model — SkyState, ramps, moon, night relight, dual-canvas grade
proposal_reviews.strengths: The solar geometry is the best-verified work in the set — I re-derived the table independently: δ=21° at φ=34.8° gives sunrise 04:58/sunset 19:02 (cosH₀=−0.2668 → H₀=105.5°), noon altitude 76.2°, noon toSun y-component +0.239 with the correctly-negated north term for the +y-south world frame. All check. The consistency contract (sun below horizon ⟺ solarLight at starlight) is proven, not asserted, and `nightFactor ≡ 1 − clamp01(solar·weatherLightMult)` with solarLight PASSED IN rather than duplicated is exactly the right anti-drift design. The weather single-fold rule (direct-kill redistributes, exposure carries weatherLightMult exactly once, probe-asserted) prevents the classic double-darkening bug before it exists. The anti-solar gibbous moon (transit 37°S at midnight — checks: 90−(34.8+18)=37.2°) with keyDir swap while both intensities ~0 is an elegant night-legibility solution. The source-atop analysis is spec-correct (blend modes composite source-over, so multiply over α=0 paints a veil — verified reasoning) and converges independently with the art-seam proposal. Phase 1 (2D-only rewire) standing alone if GL slips is good phasing. The grade() GLSL block is the right shape for the core shader to adopt.
proposal_reviews.weaknesses: The shadow march is arithmetically broken: 48 fixed 10 m steps = 480 m reach, but a 780 m ridge at 20° sun altitude throws 780/tan(20°) ≈ 2.1 km of shadow. The justification ('480 m ≈ max ridge throw at alt>9°; below that the floor is fully shadowed anyway') is wrong — mid-floor points 0.5-2 km down-sun of the east ridge are exactly the pixels the design's own marquee shot (floor in cast shadow until mid-morning) depends on, and the march terminates before reaching the occluder. The dawn money shot fails as specified. Second: the grade seam at WorldView:~602 grades everything drawn before drawNightLights — I verified suppression cues, casualty cues, fire-mission reticles, and callouts all draw before :605 — so threat crescents and bleed pools get up to 0.42-alpha navy tint at night, a behavior change vs today (only terrain+contours are night-washed; units never were). The 0.5 alpha cap is damage control, not a fix. Third: the CPU-baked RGBA8 normal texture is a second source of truth and strictly worse at close zoom than the terrain core's per-fragment normals. Minor: the table's 18:56 row claims solarLight=0.20, but the linear 17→19.5 ramp gives ~0.27 there (isNight flips ~19:06) — the direction of the claim holds but the constant is wrong.
must_fix: Replace the 48×10 m fixed-stride shadow march (480 m reach) with the terrain core's exponential map-spanning march — at 20° sun altitude a 780 m ridge shadows points 2.1 km away; as written the valley floor is incorrectly LIT at the exact hours the design's own Phase-2 acceptance shot requires it shadowed

Move the grade seam from WorldView:~602 (before drawNightLights) to after world dressing / before the tactical layer — at :602 it tints units, suppression cues, casualty cues, and callouts (all verified to draw before :605), a legibility-law violation and a silent behavior change vs today
Drop the precomputed RGBA8 normal texture; consume the terrain core's per-fragment in-shader normals (sharper at ppm 8, no second source of truth, the texelFetches are cache-resident)

Rerun the scratch probe before pinning constants: the table's solarLight(18:56)=0.20 entry is wrong (~0.27 on the linear ramp; isNight flips ~19:06, not 18:56) — harmless to the design but the probe must gate the declination/handoff numbers, not the table
River glint requires a river mask in albedo.a that no axis provisions — keep it cut (already 'cut first') unless the albedo bake explicitly reserves alpha for it

proposal_reviews.axis: atmosphere — cloud shadows, terrain-aware valley fog, aerial perspective, 2D weather evolution
proposal_reviews.strengths: The most format-disciplined proposal: every atmosphere texture is 8-bit UNORM (RG8/R8, LINEAR, REPEAT/CLAMP) — universally filterable, zero extension dependencies, 144 KB total, all cache-resident. The CPU-baked tileable two-channel FBM (modulo-lattice, fixed seed, Float32 source retained) vs live GLSL FBM is exactly the right SwiftShader-survival call: 2 fetches + smoothstep ≈ 6 ALU vs 100+. The local-valley-floor min-field is the genuinely clever idea of the set — it solves the rising-floor problem (1550→2000 m south) that a fixed MSL fog ceiling gets wrong, and the closed-form vertical transmittance is exact, not approximate, for an orthographic camera (correctly argued: path length through a pooled layer IS the thickness). The fogVisAt parity sampler over the SAME Float32 arrays the GPU samples, gated by a scratch parity harness (<0.02 on 64 probes), is the only rigorous answer in the set to the sprites-over-GL-fog problem. Sim-clock cloud advection via CPU integration (re-rolls bend streamlines instead of teleporting shadows) with wall-clock precip is a well-argued pause-semantics split. The 90 s low-pass on weather re-rolls kills the pop. Named legibility caps (CLOUD_DENSE_MAX=0.45, SYMBOLOGY_FOG_FLOOR=0.55) as constants-next-to-table is the legibility contract done right. Perf claims are honest and small (~40 ALU + 4 tiny fetches, ~0.5 ms dpr1).
proposal_reviews.weaknesses: Its biggest risk is contractual, not technical: §0 ASSUMES the terrain shader exposes worldM/elev/altNorm/N/sunVis/direct/ambient/albedo/cliff and accepts spliced GLSL chunks — but the terrain core proposal offers only a 1-tap cloud sampler and reserved fog uniforms, and exposes no cliff scalar; the mottle term needs to multiply AMBIENT inside the core's lighting combine, which requires an insertion point the core never defines. Cloud offsets are integrated mutable render state with Δclock clamped to [0,60]: a harness --hour clock-jump produces offset = seed + wind·60 — deterministic, but path-dependent vs a played-to-that-hour run; the re-seed rule on load/jump is unspecified, which will bite golden screenshots. The 'z-order identical' claim for absorbing the veil into the shader is slightly off — today's veil draws OVER decoration (WorldView:223→229) and under villages; in-shader it drops below both (small, ≤0.18 alpha, but say so). Wetness/snow non-persistence is an honestly recorded residual. Cloud-shadow-vs-relief ambiguity in stills is acknowledged with real mitigations.
must_fix: Negotiate the splice contract with the terrain core BEFORE Phase B: named chunk insertion points, the exposed locals list (including a cliff/slope scalar or its in-chunk derivation), and the ambient-mottle composition point — the core's proposed 1-tap cloud hook cannot host this design and the conflict is currently silent

Specify the cloud-offset re-seed rule for load/clock-jump (e.g. offset := f(seed, clock) on world load and on any non-monotonic clock change) so --hour harness goldens are stable and documented rather than an accident of the Δ-clamp
Correct or explicitly accept the veil z-order change: today's veil draws over decoration; in-shader it moves below decoration and villages — one line in the design plus a Phase-B screenshot note

proposal_reviews.axis: art-seam — sprite shadows, decoration, grade coherence, contours, hero assets, ART_BIBLE contract
proposal_reviews.strengths: The shadow-strip pipeline is excellent production engineering: data-cast-shadow groups stripped at manifest build (sources stay the edited artifact, per the generated-files invariant), with castHeight ⟺ group presence as BUILD ERRORS — both failure modes (double shadow / missing shadow) become compile-time. The P1-at-fixed-legacy-NW-sun phase is the single best phasing idea in the set: the entire SVG strip + runtime-shadow mechanism QAs as a pure screenshot-diff against today's baselines, fully decoupled from GL. The HESCO/ECP catch (rotated statics at draw.ts:404,445 already violate the baked-SE contract today; world-axis projection after opts.rot fixes them for free) is a genuine latent-bug find. The relief-inversion flag — a real south noon sun on a north-up map is the classic cartographic inversion condition — with the concrete 25-35% fixed NW form-light recommendation is expert-level perception knowledge the GL axes lack. The grade-seam placement (world dressing graded, units/ink/FX above — verified to match today's behavior where the wash never touched units) is the correct legibility call, and the drawCopNightLights split is a thoughtful detail. Worst-case cost is stated honestly (+1800 blits ≈ +2-4 ms) with pre-wired escape hatches (two-pass, cap, per-bucket atlas), and shadows self-gate off at night/overcast via shadowAlpha.
proposal_reviews.weaknesses: It forks two things other axes own better. (1) A third sun model — δ=+15°, solar noon 12:15 — disagreeing with both other proposals (δ=20/12:00 and δ=21/12:00); its 'hand-verified' numbers are also looser (claims sunset ~19:05; δ=15/noon-12:15 actually gives ~18:58). Three suns is the worst synthesis outcome possible. (2) Its fog position ('occluding fog must live on the TOP canvas; GL fog would have qalats poking through') directly contradicts the atmosphere axis and is the weaker design — it keeps the drawWeather blobs that the atmosphere axis correctly identifies as the placeholder for the real pooled fog, and the qalat-poking objection is already answered by fogVisAt alpha fades with parity-harness rigor. (3) The 'binding parity rule' that GL grade MUST be the identical alpha-mix form ('NOT a multiply, or the canvases drift') is technically wrong-headed: terrain needs exposure/WB/saturation, which mix-toward-tint cannot express; perceptual parity via a shared table + calibration screenshots is the right contract, formula identity is not. gradeFor() returning only an rgba tint is sufficient for sprites but not for terrain. Hero-asset hours (8-15 h) are honest; the shadow-mask memory (+4-5 MB) and bake time (+60-150 ms) are accounted.
must_fix: Delete the third sun model (δ=+15°, solar noon 12:15) and consume the shared sky module's SunState/spriteShadow output — the declination/noon constants must not fork across canvases, and the sky axis's δ=21/noon-12:00 is the numerically verified one

Drop the binding GL-must-use-alpha-mix parity mandate; replace with: both canvases read one altitude-keyed table, GL applies the full grade block, 2D applies the source-atop tint, and the 06:00/12:00/17:30/22:00 calibration screenshots (already in the plan) are the acceptance gate

Cede fog occlusion to the atmosphere axis (floor-field GL fog + fogVisAt sprite fades, parity-harness gated); cut the drawWeather blob pooling weight and fogDensityAt — keep only the drawWeather reorder so precip draws above structures

Ship sprite shadows default-on only after the promised shoot.mjs --fps before/after at the dense-forest worst case, with the two-pass/cap escape hatch already implemented behind a flag, not merely described

cross_axis_conflicts.between: terrain-core vs sky/ToD vs art-seam
cross_axis_conflicts.conflict: Three sun models in three files with three sets of constants: lib/render/gl/sun.ts (δ=+20°, noon 12:00), lib/render/atmosphere.ts (δ=+21°, noon 12:00, + moon + colors + spriteShadow), lib/render/sun.ts (δ=+15°, noon 12:15). Sprite shadows pointing differently than ridge shadows is worse than no shadows — art-seam itself says so.
cross_axis_conflicts.resolution: ONE module: the sky axis's atmosphere.ts skyState() wins — it is the only numerically verified model (table re-derived and confirmed), has the richest output (sun+moon+keyDir+grade+spriteShadow+nightFactor), and the cleanest anti-drift design (solarLight passed in, never duplicated). Terrain core consumes sunDir/keyDir as uniforms; art-seam consumes spriteShadow. δ=+21°, solar noon 12:00, pinned with the scratch-sun-probe as the gate. Owner's open question on campaign month: any δ in 15-23° works, but pin it in ONE place.

cross_axis_conflicts.between: sky/ToD vs art-seam vs terrain-core
cross_axis_conflicts.conflict: Who applies the color grade, in what form, at which seam. Sky: rich in-shader grade (exposure/WB/sat/lift) + 2D source-atop tint inserted at WorldView:~602, which grades units/cues/callouts (verified: all draw before :605). Art-seam: single rgba tint via gradeFor(), seam after world dressing with units ABOVE it, plus a mandate that GL use the identical alpha-mix form. Terrain core: only a gain/lift hook, which can express neither.
cross_axis_conflicts.resolution: Composite resolution: GL terrain gets the sky axis's full grade() block (gain/lift hook deleted); the 2D canvas gets the source-atop tint (both proposals independently converged on source-atop with correct spec reasoning — adopt); the seam goes where art-seam puts it (after decoration/villages/COP/weather, BEFORE markers/units/orders/FX/HUD) because that matches today's behavior and the legibility law; the alpha-mix-parity mandate is dropped in favor of one shared altitude-keyed table + the 4-hour calibration screenshot gate. Both tint tables merge into atmosphere.ts.

cross_axis_conflicts.between: atmosphere vs art-seam vs terrain-core
cross_axis_conflicts.conflict: Fog ownership and the occlusion model. Atmosphere: pooled fog in the GL terrain shader (floor-field + closed-form transmittance) with sprite coherence via fogVisAt alpha fades over the same Float32 arrays. Art-seam: 'occluding fog must live on the TOP canvas' via upgraded drawWeather blobs; GL keeps only non-occluding haze. Terrain core: a simple u_fogTopElev/density/color uniform hook.
cross_axis_conflicts.resolution: Atmosphere wins outright: its floor-field + exp-transmittance is physically exact for this camera, its parity harness makes the sprite-mismatch risk measurable (<0.02 on 64 probes), and its per-class floors encode legibility as named constants. Art-seam's qalats-poking-through objection is answered by the fogVisAt fades (scenery fades fully, symbology floors at 0.55). The blobs die per atmosphere's plan; the terrain core's simple fog uniforms are superseded by the spliced chunk. Keep art-seam's drawWeather reorder (precip above structures) — it is orthogonal and cheap.

cross_axis_conflicts.between: terrain-core vs sky/ToD
cross_axis_conflicts.conflict: Two shadow passes with different march math, thresholds, and claimed ownership: terrain core (1024² R8 FBO, 56 exponential steps spanning the map, >0.25°/≤4 Hz, sun only) vs sky (48×10 m = 480 m reach — arithmetically insufficient, >0.5°, keyDir with sun↔moon swap, claims the policy and the GLSL while terrain claims the pass). Sky's own open question flags the file-ownership collision.
cross_axis_conflicts.resolution: Terrain core owns the pass, the FBO, and the march (its exponential stride is the only one that reaches a 2 km shadow throw); sky owns the policy inputs: keyDir (the moon swap is the night feature and must survive), the rebake threshold (0.25° vs 0.5° — decide by eyeballing the shadow-line stepping at 60× warp in Phase 3), and the per-frame combine semantics (shadowStrength floor so shadowed ground keeps full ambient). One writer: lib/render/gl/terrain-gl.ts + shaders.ts belong to terrain core; sky delivers keyDir/threshold/strength through SkyState.

cross_axis_conflicts.between: terrain-core vs atmosphere
cross_axis_conflicts.conflict: Integration surface for cloud shadows and fog: terrain core 'reserves' a 1-tap cloud sampler (1×1 white default) and flat fog uniforms so 'axes extend TerrainEnv, never the shader plumbing'; atmosphere's design needs two scrolled octave fetches, coverage thresholding, sun-parallax by per-pixel elevation, a mottle term on AMBIENT, and a cliff scalar — none of which fit through one tap, and atmosphere's §0 assumes a chunk-splice contract the core never offers.
cross_axis_conflicts.resolution: Adopt atmosphere's chunk model: the core terrain shader is assembled from axis-owned GLSL chunks (atmosphere.glsl.ts spliced at named insertion points) with a documented locals contract (worldM, elev, altNorm, N, sunVis, direct, ambient, albedo, cliff derived from the normal's dz). The core's 1-tap hook is deleted as insufficient; its uniform-contract discipline (fixed texture units, defaulted uniforms) survives as the convention for the chunks. The lighting combine line moves to: lit = albedo*(direct*sunVis*cloudShadow + ambient*cloudMottle), then applyAtmosphere, then grade — order pinned in the contract.

cross_axis_conflicts.between: terrain-core vs atmosphere
cross_axis_conflicts.conflict: Both write the altitude warm/cool + haze replacement for topo.ts:296-309: terrain core §7 as 'default parameterization' in the core shader, atmosphere §4 as its own applyAtmosphere with weather/zoom awareness. Same lines, two owners; if both land, haze double-applies — atmosphere's own named risk.
cross_axis_conflicts.resolution: One owner: atmosphere owns applyAtmosphere (its version is a strict superset — same default coefficients 0.08/0.13/~10%, plus visibilityM and ppm zoomBoost). Terrain core ships those constants only as the Phase-2 defaults inside the atmosphere chunk's slot, deleted from the bake in the same commit the GL path activates (atmosphere Phase B). The bake-side deletion (topo.ts:296-309) and the shade-term deletion (169-173) are listed together in the bakeAlbedo spec so neither double-applies.

cross_axis_conflicts.between: terrain-core vs sky/ToD vs art-seam
cross_axis_conflicts.conflict: Night-wash lifecycle: terrain core keeps the 2D wash through Phases 1-3 ('night regression impossible') with a u_nightMix hook; sky deletes it and relights with real moonlight; art-seam replaces it with the source-atop grade pass using today's exact constants. Three different end states for topo.ts:587-592 (verified: wash draws after contours, before decoration — so today trees/qalats render full-bright at night, as art-seam observes).
cross_axis_conflicts.resolution: Sequence, don't choose: (1) terrain core lands with the wash intact on the 2D path — correct transitional state; (2) the grade/night landing (one coordinated commit: art-seam's reorder + grade pass + sky's moonlit GL relight) deletes the wash in exactly one place, replacing it with sky's moon-key lighting on terrain and the tint pass on world dressing. Sky's nightFactor ≡ 1−ambientLight() keeps drawNightLights' ≤0.25 gate bit-identical throughout. The core's u_nightMix hook is subsumed by the moon term in the combine — drop it from the contract.

cross_axis_conflicts.between: terrain-core vs atmosphere
cross_axis_conflicts.conflict: Snow ownership: terrain core keeps the 68% snow cap baked into the albedo ('character survives pixel-for-pixel'); atmosphere prefers snow in-shader so the dynamic snow line (68%→40% during Snow weather) has no visible seam at the baked cap edge.
cross_axis_conflicts.resolution: Keep snow baked through the core's ship (lowest porting risk, the cap is part of the tuned character); atmosphere's accumulation extra uses its own band-restricted variant (dynamic snow only in the 0.40-0.68 band below the baked cap — atmosphere explicitly supports this layout). Promote snow to full shader ownership only if the cap-edge seam is visible in the Phase-E screenshots. Same deferral logic for wetness: uWet multiplies albedo, no bake change needed.

cross_axis_conflicts.between: sky/ToD vs terrain-core
cross_axis_conflicts.conflict: Normal sourcing: sky precomputes normals CPU-side into an RGBA8 texture ('8-bit normals are fine at 5 m cells'); terrain core computes them per-fragment in-shader from the height texture (bake's exact forward-difference) and explicitly rejected a normal texture as a second source of truth.
cross_axis_conflicts.resolution: Terrain core wins: per-fragment normals are screen-resolution sharp at ppm 8 (a fixed 512² normal map is not), cost ~12 L2-resident texelFetches, and keep one source of truth registered to the contours drawn from the same elev array. Sky's RGBA8 normal texture is cut; its lighting combine consumes the core's normalAt().

cross_axis_conflicts.between: atmosphere vs everyone (pause semantics)
cross_axis_conflicts.conflict: Only atmosphere specifies clock semantics for animated atmosphere: sim-clock integrated cloud advection (frozen at pause, racing at warp) vs wall-clock precip particles. The core says only 'paused game never flickers'; sky's grade and art-seam's shadows are pure functions of secondsOfDay (implicitly sim-clock); today's drawWeather is wall-clock phase.
cross_axis_conflicts.resolution: Adopt atmosphere's split as the binding rule for all axes: world-anchored phenomena (sun, shadows, clouds, fog depth, sprite shadows, grade) follow world.secondsOfDay; screen-space ephemera (precip streaks) stay wall-clock so the UI never looks hung during pause. Add atmosphere's must-fix: a documented offset re-seed on load/clock-jump so --hour harness goldens are deterministic.

best_ideas_to_graft: Terrain core's bit-faithful heightAt port of Terrain.elevAt (R32F + NEAREST + manual 4-texelFetch bilinear, cell-corner lattice, clamp size-1.001) — the registration guarantee that keeps 2D contours glued to GL relief; verified against the cited code

Terrain core's unlit-albedo hybrid: CPU bake minus the lighting/grade/haze terms (verified strict subset of shipping code), 26-class character preserved pixel-for-pixel, GPU albedo bake deferred behind a perceptual-diff gate — the hash2 non-portability argument is real (confirmed: int32 product exceeds 2^53)

Terrain core's Phase-1 GL-blit-parity step + the alive 2D fallback path selected at one branch — proves canvas stack/DPR/camera math before any lighting exists and keeps every --disable-gpu harness baseline valid forever

Terrain core's rebaked shadow FBO with exponential stride (5·1.13^k, map-spanning) — the only shadow march in the set that actually reaches a 2 km ridge throw; one bilinear tap per frame, ≤4 Hz amortized

Sky axis's verified solar model (δ=+21°, φ=34.8°, the negated-north world-frame mapping) plus the scratch-sun-probe asserting sun-below-horizon ⟺ solarLight-at-starlight and nightFactor ≡ 1−ambientLight() across 24 h × 6 weathers — consistency as a tested contract, not a comment

Sky axis's weather single-fold rule: weatherLightMult enters exposure exactly once; weather's other effect is direct/ambient REDISTRIBUTION (directMult kills the beam and with it cast shadows) — prevents double-darkening by construction, probe-asserted
Sky axis's anti-solar gibbous moon with keyDir sun↔moon swap while both intensities are ~0 — night relief with real raking shadows instead of a navy veil, weather-killed exactly like the sun
Sky axis's grade() GLSL block (exposure, per-channel WB, saturation, shadow-lift) as the terrain shader's grade stage with identity defaults

The convergent source-atop finding (sky + art-seam independently, both with correct compositing-spec reasoning): the ONLY canvas op that tints drawn pixels while preserving alpha on the transparent-backed top canvas — multiply/overlay would veil the GL terrain through the transparent regions

Atmosphere's local-valley-floor min-field (128² R8) + closed-form vertical transmittance — fog that pools in the rising river draw and tributaries, exact for an orthographic camera, one fetch + one exp()

Atmosphere's fogVisAt parity sampler: the 2D layer samples the SAME retained Float32 arrays the GPU textures were uploaded from, gated by scratch-atmo-parity.ts (<0.02 on 64 probes) — the only rigorous sprites-in-fog answer
Atmosphere's CPU-baked tileable RG8 cloud tile (fixed seed, modulo lattice) — 2 fetches + smoothstep instead of 100+ ALU live FBM; the SwiftShader-survival decision
Atmosphere's sim-clock cloud advection by CPU integration (re-rolls bend streamlines, never teleport) / wall-clock precip split, and the 90 s low-pass on all weather-driven params
Atmosphere's named legibility caps next to the table: CLOUD_DENSE_MAX=0.45, SYMBOLOGY_FOG_FLOOR=0.55, CONTOUR_FOG_FLOOR=0.65, VEIL_A_MAX=0.18, base wavelength ≥1200 m

Art-seam's data-cast-shadow strip pipeline with build-time castHeight ⟺ group cross-validation — both failure modes (double shadow / hollowed art) become build errors; sources stay the single edited artifact
Art-seam's P1-at-fixed-legacy-NW-sun phase: the entire sprite-shadow mechanism QAs as a pure screenshot-diff against today's baselines, fully decoupled from GL — the best de-risking move in the set
Art-seam's HESCO/ECP rotated-static fix (projection in world axes after opts.rot) — repairs a verified latent bug (draw.ts:404,445) as a measurable delta

Art-seam's relief-inversion warning + the reserve fixed-NW form-light uniform (default 0, enabled only if noon screenshots invert) — cartographic perception knowledge the GL axes lack, kept as a calibration lever rather than a baked-in compromise

Art-seam's grade-seam placement (world dressing graded; units/cues/ink/FX above — verified to match today's wash behavior) and the drawCopNightLights split so life-sign glows stay luminous over the dim
